comparisons.peer_topic: Gross margin financial results and VMware impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased to $32,509 million in fiscal year 2024 from $24,690 million in fiscal year 2023, primarily due to VMware contributions offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by the same amortization factors, less favorable semiconductor product mix, and offsets from infrastructure software margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom (AVGO) report 2024 gross margin percentages and attribute the primary drivers to product mix and specific segment contributions, though their trends diverged significantly. AMD reported an increase in gross margin to 49% from 46%, driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards higher-margin Data Center and Client revenues. In contrast, AVGO saw its gross margin percentage decrease to 63% from 69%, primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix, despite an increase in total gross margin dollars. While both cite 'product mix' as a factor, AMD's was favorable and drove margin expansion, whereas AVGO's was less favorable and contributed to margin contraction alongside acquisition-related amortization.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron (MU) discuss 2024 gross margin performance in the context of prior year pressures, but with opposite outcomes and drivers. AMD improved its gross margin to 49% in 2024 from 46% in 2023, driven by a favorable shift in revenue mix towards Data Center and Client segments. In contrast, MU significantly improved its gross margin to 22% in 2024 from negative 9% in 2023, driven by increases in average selling prices (ASPs) for DRAM and NAND products and manufacturing cost reductions, following significant inventory write-downs in the prior year. While both show improvement, AMD's driver is mix-driven margin expansion in a generally healthy environment, whereas MU's is a recovery from significant prior-year losses due to price and cost factors.
